Let $f(x)=2x-{x}^{3}.$ Computing the derivative ${f}^{′}(x)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x-{x}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3}) \\  & =2-3{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We then compute ${f}^{′}(1)$, which gives

$$
{f}^{′}(1)=2-3({1}^{2})=-1.
$$

Finally, we use the point-slope form with $m=-1$ and the coordinates of our point $(1,1),$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =(-1)(x-1) \\ y & =-x+1+1 \\ y & =-x+2.\end{aligned}
$$
